q1: SELECT beer.name, min_price, bar FROM beer LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT beer, MIN(price) AS min_price FROM serves GROUP BY beer) AS t ON beer.name = t.beer LEFT OUTER JOIN serves ON beer.name = serves.beer AND min_price = serves.price
q2: SELECT beer.name AS beer, MIN(s.price) AS price, CASE WHEN NOT MIN(s.price) IS NULL THEN GROUP_CONCAT(bar.name, ', ') ELSE NULL END AS bar FROM beer LEFT JOIN serves AS s ON beer.name = s.beer LEFT JOIN bar ON s.bar = bar.name GROUP BY beer.name ORDER BY beer.name

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 uses a subquery to find the minimum price for each beer and then joins it with the 'serves' table to find the corresponding bar, while Q2 uses a GROUP BY clause to find the minimum price for each beer and then uses a CASE statement to find the corresponding bar. The difference arises when there are multiple bars serving the same beer at the same price, as Q1 will return all such bars, while Q2 will only return one of them.
counterexample_dsp: A test case where a beer is served by two bars at the same minimum price.
